name: music-school
estimated: how thick its canopy and its roofs are, how deep the auditorium's fascia is, the size of its window's frames and head and how far they stand out, the radius of its downpipes, where the lower steps of its parapet to the car park begin (to about 0.25 m), how high the steps between the LiDAR's levels stand (equal rises), and the colour of the walls no photograph shows

building.title: Music School, University of Auckland
building.note: outline: building 250's outer ring from the main project's campus.json, moved at one vertex where Te Pūtahi Tangata (201) stands near it (building.outline_note), in the map's frame; it chooses the crop box and the building's own points (frame.near_outline, measure and topview). campus_outline: the campus.json ring as it is, kept for the record; the site replaces block 250 by its id.
building.outline_note: campus_outline with one vertex moved: vertex 8 (232.7, 134.3) 0.3 m into the building, to (232.99, 134.36), so that within frame.near_outline (1.5 m) none of Te Pūtahi Tangata's (201) returns count as 250's: its outline stands 0.44 m from 250's at the west, and with campus_outline the data stage took one of its returns (20.24 m above 32.7, inside 201's outline). With this ring it takes 14,578 returns more than 3 m up, none of 201's, and loses none of 250's own. The Overbridge (202), whose outline meets 250's along its south-east and south sides and overlaps it (74 of the crop's returns lie inside both), is a walkway under a slatted roof: its returns stand 2.0-2.5 m above 32.7 at the most (595 on its south-east branch, p95 2.36), under frame.min_above (3 m), so none of them is selected and the ring needs no trim there; the 266 selected returns within 0.5 m of its outline stand 3.5-9.5 m up, 250's walls and eaves over it. The house east of the car park (not on the campus map) stands more than 1.5 m off: none of its returns is selected.

origin.note: the campus origin, as in campus.json; the landmark's local metres = NZTM (EPSG:2193) minus the NZTM of this point, with grid north

door.note: view frame: the point whose ground is the model's y = 0, where place.py meets the map's ground. The foot of the face to the car park, 0.6 m out from the canopy's edge, near its middle, where the LiDAR's ground is 32.68 m (38 ground returns within 1 m: 32.61-32.78 for p10-p90), 0.02 m from the frame's ground. The photographs show no door on that face (cars stand before its foot); the ground before it falls from +1.03 at its north-west end to -0.96 before the auditorium.

frame.method: LiDAR building points (class 6) more than min_above m above the ground and within near_outline m of building.outline (building.outline_note: none of 201's or 202's): centre = mean x/y of those higher than tower_above m (3 m: all of them, so the centre of the roofs round the courtyard); axis = the bearing of most of the walls seen from above (axis_from walls), of the two square to each other the one nearest the principal axis of all the building's points (spine_below 30 m, spine_radius 45 m: the whole building), pointing south-east (bearing 135.55 deg); toStreet = the axis turned 90 deg toward street_side: north-east (45.55 deg), to the car park and the panorama qru8. The screening's frame (tower_above 5.8, street_side west) put +z to the south-west, away from the car park.

streetview.pano_ids_note: qru8 (2022-09, 33.8 m from the centre, 9.3 m out from the face to the car park, at x 19.4, z 27.7 of the view frame) sees that face whole, from the north corner to the canopy's south-east end, and the auditorium's ochre wall beyond it at a slant: the screening's sight-line test over the LiDAR gives its faces toward the camera 98-100%. Its 143 tiles were bought for this building on 2026-11-02 (22:24-22:26 NZDT) through the ledger. 2LAG (2022-09, 30.2 m from the centre, at x 6.3, z 29.5), which also sees this face, at the canopy's south-east end, and the ochre wall at about 33 deg, was bought in round 2 (143 tiles, 2026-11-02 23:08-23:10 NZDT) for a squarer view of that wall's window. It is not pinned: its photographs stand turned about 8 deg in the cut (its recorded tilt 85.85 deg and roll 2.76 deg) and its camera is not fitted, so nothing is measured or scored through it. Pinned for one compare (round 2, through its recorded camera, which the refine stage does not correct: 14% sky round the model's silhouette), its views gave IoU in the box 0.738, 0.708 and 0.801 and luma medians 244 against 231-232: the same wall reads 231-232 in its photographs and 245-248 in qru8's, a difference of exposure. Both copyrights read "From the Owner, Photo by: Google".
streetview.camera_fixes_note: [x, z, pitch, yaw, roll] (landmarks/README.md). qru8 (round 1, 2026-11-02): z, pitch and roll fitted to the photograph's own edges in the wide view, the parapet's treads against the sky, each a level line on the parapet's face (z 16.42) at its height: the long top at 8.3 m (the LiDAR's, x 17.5-22.2: 8.26-8.45) and the three treads below it, which the photograph shows as four levels in equal rises between the LiDAR's 6.74 (x 11-15) and 8.3, so 7.13, 7.52 and 7.91 (the LiDAR's highest returns in 0.5 m bins over x 15-17.5: 7.07-7.99). Level lines on one face cannot tell the yaw from the roll, so the yaw is held at the recorded heading (0): fitted on the first cut -1.12 and +2.27 (rms 0.7 px over 318 points), cut again level by the roll and fitted again: pitch -0.02, roll +0.02, rms 2.8 px over 330 points (0.3-0.9 px on the three upper treads; a few columns of the lowest, against Te Pūtahi Tangata behind it, are off by more). The panorama records a tilt of 87.99 deg and a roll of -0.85 deg, at this view's 53 deg off the car's heading of the same size, though the fit uses the photograph alone. Level lines cannot place x either: it is set where the risers between the treads, which the photograph shows at x 16.28, 17.04 and 17.84 through the recorded x (19.36), best fit the LiDAR's returns on the parapet's top (27 returns over x 14.5-19.5 at z 15.7-16.9: their median distance from the steps' tops 0.07 m with the camera 0.2 to 0.6 m toward -x, 0.17 m at the recorded x): 0.4 m toward -x, 18.96, which puts the risers at x 15.88, 16.64 and 17.44. Round 2 (2026-11-02): the yaw and x from two vertical edges of known place, the ochre wall's two corners on the LiDAR's wall lines (x -8.66 and -17.59 at z 15.64: 169 wall returns at z p50 15.63), five and three points down each in the wide view as cut now, with the treads: with x held the yaw is -0.32 deg (the edges 0.5 px rms), with x free x 19.12 (sd 0.13) and yaw -0.22 (sd 0.08), the edges 0.6 px and the treads unchanged (2.8 px); all five free, x 19.24, z 27.48, pitch -0.14, yaw -0.40, roll -0.37, each within about 1.5 sd of the four held. So x 19.12 and yaw -0.22, where the risers then land at x 16.09, 16.84 and 17.64 (the LiDAR's returns on the parapet's top fit risers there as well as at round 1's: 0.07 m median for the camera 0.2-0.6 m toward -x of the recorded place). The views are cut as before (the yaw and x do not change the cut): byte-identical. 2LAG (2022-09; its 143 tiles bought for this building on 2026-11-02, 23:08-23:10 NZDT, through the ledger) records a tilt of 85.85 deg and a roll of 2.76 deg, and its photographs stand turned about 8 deg in the cut; its camera is not fitted, and nothing is measured through it: its photograph shows the ochre wall's window squarer than qru8's (four lights, two rows, a white head), and the house before it hides the window's lower row.
